### ✅ Key Insight

A number `n` is a **power of two** if and only if it satisfies the condition:

```cpp
n > 0 && (n & (n - 1)) == 0
```

### ✅ Efficient Solution

Here is a clean and efficient C++ implementation that prints all numbers **not** powers of two up to a given upper limit (e.g., `1e6`):

```cpp
#include <iostream>

    return n > 0 && (n & (n - 1)) == 0;

    for (long long i = 3; i <= upperLimit; ++i) {
        if (!isPowerOfTwo(i)) {

        }
    }

}
```
